newsitem.title: CHINA: China's diesel prices slump in early 1997.
newsitem.headline: China's diesel prices slump in early 1997.

text.p: Rising domestic stockpiles and declining international prices have caused China's diesel prices to drop sharply in early 1997, the Market Daily said on Friday.
The average price for diesel had fallen to below 2,600 yuan per tonne after international prices began to slump in January, the newspaper said but gave no direct comparative figures.

In some parts of the country, shortages had driven diesel prices as high as 4,000 yuan a tonne before imports increased late last year. Prices later stabilised at around 2,900 yuan after refineries stepped up production.
Diesel prices in the southern province of Guangdong dropped to about 2,200 yuan per tonne from 2,800 yuan at the end of 1996, while in central China they slid to 2,300 yuan.

In the southwestern province of Sichuan, wholesale diesel fuel prices had fallen 314 yuan since the end of last year, while in eastern China's Jiangsu province prices fell by 170 yuan a tonne, it said but gave no figures for current prices.
The newspaper attributed the drop in prices to a glut caused by huge imports and rising domestic output.
China began increasing imports in December to ease domestic shortages and about 2.0 million tonnes of diesel fuel had arrived since early 1997, it said.
Beijing had also raised the official ex-refinery price of diesel twice in the fourth quarter of 1996 to stimulate domestic output, it said.
China planned to produce 48 million tonnes of diesel in 1997, up by 5.5 million tonnes or 11 percent from last year, it said.
China produced 7.41 million tonnes of diesel in the first two months of 1997, up 9.3 percent compared with the year-ago period, State Statistical Bureau figures showed.
China produced 3.56 million tonnes of diesel in February, the figures showed.
